item: One unreadable link or sitemap loc no longer ends a source's crawl, and a sitemap's page locs are held to the source's host (R626, R627)
summary: R626 and R627 (Plan's rulings on two findings of R624's read, one PR after R624). BEFORE: urllib.parse raises a bare ValueError on an href or loc such as http://[::1 (an unclosed IPv6 bracket), a stray ']', a bracketed host that is no address (http://[foo]/) or a netloc NFKC would change. src/ingest/crawl.py _harvest_links let it out of urljoin, which ended the whole crawl of the source; discover_sitemap_urls let it out of urlparse(sm_url) in the child check (index children and robots-declared sitemaps alike), which ended the whole discovery; and a urlset's page locs were handed on unread, so the caller's ingest_url raised it from EthicalFetcher.fetch and the walk of the rest of the sitemap's pages ended (the crawl rung logged the source as failed and rolled it back, the qualification trial counted an error). And a urlset's page locs were never host-checked (only child sitemaps were), so a sitemap could make the app fetch pages on other sites and store them as the source's. NOW: _harvest_links (crawl.py:137) skips an href it cannot read and hands it back; crawl_source counts the distinct ones over the whole crawl (crawl.py:238, :264) in CrawlReport.skipped_unreadable, also in to_dict (crawl.py:103, :112). Both checks in discover_sitemap_urls call ONE comparison, _off_host (sitemap.py:153): None when urlparse cannot read the URL, else the child sitemaps' rule, _registrable_host(netloc) != base_host. An unreadable child or page loc is counted in SitemapDiscoveryReport.skipped_unreadable (sitemap.py:206, :257, :298); an off-host page loc goes to skipped_off_host, written through failure_url (sitemap.py:296-301), and is never returned. Page locs are de-duplicated before the check, so each distinct loc is counted once. The other parses on these paths were gone through and never raise: _registrable_host and the host key catch the ValueError of .port, canonicalize_url catches everything, a link that reaches the fetcher has been read by urlparse already, and a URL urlparse reads but the fetcher cannot (a port out of range) is refused by the fetcher before any request, as before (a crawl tallies it fetch_failed). R627's EFFECT ('same rule' is the host minus www., not the registrable domain), from the bundled catalogues (6,731 sources in configs/sources.yml, academic_sources.yml, legal_sources_generated.yml, sources_spectrum.yml, official_sources.yml; none names a sitemap, they are found at run time; with markets_sources.yml and legal_sources.yml, which the seeder also loads, 7,118 rows and 969 subdomains, and those two add no feed on another subdomain and no Unicode domain): 906 have a domain that is itself a subdomain (edition.cnn.com, english.elpais.com, asia.nikkei.com, folha.uol.com.br, news.sky.com), whose sitemap pages on the parent domain or a sibling are now skipped; 176 have their feed on another subdomain of their own domain, 98 of them on a feed or service host (rss., export., feeds., cdn., api. and the like) and 78 (some among those 906) on a non-infrastructure one (kyodonews.net to english.kyodonews.net, yna.co.kr to en.yna.co.kr, radio-canada.ca to ici.radio-canada.ca, m.radiochisinau.md to radiochisinau.md, english.vov.vn to vov.vn, 22 erudit.org journals to www.erudit.org), the likeliest to list pages on another host of their domain; 3 have a Unicode domain (åa.no and two others), and _registrable_host does not IDNA-encode, so their pages written in punycode were off the host (ruled a defect, R631, fixed below); the 29 statistics agencies all match. No existing test lists a page off its source's host (test_sitemap, test_crawl_supplement, test_stop_is_not_an_outcome, R624's), so none changed. The crawl's own link check already refused every one of these, so the sitemap and the crawl now agree. TESTS: tests/test_sitemap_scope_unreadable_r626_r627.py, 64, through the real crawl_source, discover_sitemap_urls, sitemap_trial_ingest and the crawl rung (_lane_step_crawl) with a real EthicalFetcher over an in-memory session (every planted off-site page routed, so a fetch is seen). 37 fail on local/r624 4c28b7e74: seven unreadable hrefs among good links (the good ones crawled, the bad one counted), a count once per crawl and on a page that is no article, seven unreadable page locs and seven unreadable index children, an unreadable robots-declared sitemap, five off-host page locs (another host, the source's name as a label, a suffix, a userinfo before the last @ listed masked, an IPv6 literal), the same off-host loc listed once and the same unreadable loc counted once, a subdomain page loc, a loc with no host, the Unicode/punycode case, the trial walking past an unreadable loc and never fetching an off-host one, and the crawl rung crawling the source (it failed it before). 27 pass there, all controls: a bracket in a relative path followed, a port out of range never requested and never ending the crawl or the trial, a page of readable links, the helpers never raising on any case, the source host however spelled (www., capitals, :443, :8443, http, an @ in the path or query), a www. source keeping its bare-host pages, an off-host child still listed and never fetched. 16 mutants, none survived (the harvest guard, the href not recorded, the page's set not gathered, the count not written, to_dict without it, a count per page; _off_host's guard, each check's skip and count, the page check undone, off-host page locs kept, the raw loc listed, the de-dup only for kept locs, the netloc compared by hand). 1,895 passed across the crawl, sitemap, R620/R621/R624, SSRF, network-consent, sink-sweep, repo-invariants and every other test that drives crawl or sitemap; the one failure (test_shared_file_writes: src/ingest/__init__.py:416/548/712) fails the same on 4c28b7e74. NOT CHANGED: the counts live on the two report objects only, where skipped_off_host already was: nothing reads skipped_off_host into an API response, a log line or the UI (the crawl rung reads urls and pages_fetched; the trial's result, which carries discovered/attempted/tally/errors, is discarded by qualification.py:1754; archive_backfill.py reads urls), so no chrome string was added. The off-host entries and the error lines are written through failure_url (R624's fold). After R624 and R630 are merged in, _off_host calls R624's _off_site, so a child sitemap or a page loc whose netloc holds an @ is off the host on both checks (R630), and crawl_source skips a harvested link carrying a userinfo before its scope check, whatever the scope (R630). The RSS feed pass had the same bug one layer down, found by this build: ingest_source (pipeline.py:633) hands an item link such as http://[::1 (feedparser passes it through, checked) to ingest_url, and EthicalFetcher.fetch's own urlparse (src/ingest/__init__.py) raised the bare ValueError, ending that source's feed pass. fetch() now refuses such a URL as an unsupported or malformed URL (FetchFailed, raised outside the handler, nothing requested), which ingest_url records as that item's failure; it covers every caller of fetch(). 9 tests: each of the 7 unreadable forms refused with nothing requested, a feed with an unreadable link between two good ones stores both, and a control (an ftp URL refused as before); 8 fail on the parent commit, the control passes; two mutants (the None not refused; the ValueError re-raised) killed. An unreadable crawl start URL or source domain still raises (configuration, not the host's text; the rung isolates it per source). R631 (the coordinator's ruling on that effect, folded here): the same-site comparison read the host as written, so a source whose domain is written in Unicode lost every punycode link, child sitemap and page loc, and a punycode source the Unicode ones; a crawl of a Unicode-domain source lost its own links too, since requests sends the punycode host and answers with a punycode URL. NOW: _off_site (crawl.py), which the crawl and the sitemap's _off_host both use, compares crawl.py _site_key of both sides: an ASCII host as it is (lower-cased by urllib.parse), a non-ASCII one encoded as requests encodes it before connecting (idna.encode(host, uts46=True), PreparedRequest._get_idna_encoded_host). A host that cannot be encoded (an empty label, a label over 63, a name over 253, a disallowed character; idna refuses a 10 MB name at once) is None and off the site, even against its own text: fail closed. Stated: UTS 46 keeps ß as xn--zca (not IDNA 2003's ss) and maps a fullwidth letter to its ASCII one, so such a link reads as on the site, as the connection would go; the fetcher's own parser check (R622's _refuse_parser_mismatch) refuses both kinds of name before any request. Tests (both directions for the helper with www. and capitals, a sitemap's page locs and an index child in the other form, a crawl kept to one site following its own links in the other form and still not the evil one, four unencodable hosts off the site and never a crash, a crawl that skips such a link and walks the rest, the encoding pinned to requests', an ASCII control): 17, 89 in the file; on the parent commit the 16 new cases fail and the control and the other 72 pass; the stated-effect test that pinned the punycode loss is replaced. Mutants: 8, 7 killed (either side not encoded; None compared as a value; IDNA 2003; idna without UTS 46; the error answered with the raw host; ASCII hosts encoded too); the 8th, UTS 46 transitional, is equivalent on idna 3.20, which ignores that deprecated flag. idna becomes a declared core dependency, idna>=3.7,<4 (Steward 3's read: crawl.py is the first direct import in src, and it came only through requests): 3.7 is the first release without the quadratic idna.encode on crafted input (CVE-2024-3651), and crawl.py hands it hosts from fetched pages. requirements.lock already pins idna 3.18 (via requests, httpx and anyio), so no pin moves; the next pip-compile adds the project to its via list. Two more mutants were dropped as equivalent with the code they tested: a separate None check on the site side, and a 253-character cap before the encoder (removed, since idna refuses such a name at once). THE INDEPENDENT READ (Opus, of cd07c6021 and of R631 at a24de7254): GO, with no scope escape (2,229,984 locs through a recording adapter: 0 off-host connections, 2,880 on the base) and no exception that ends a pass; its four should-fixes are folded. (S1) archive_backfill.advance_backfill walked a URL list saved by an older build as it stood, so a list enumerated before R627 kept fetching and storing its off-host locs: each saved URL now goes through _off_host first (archive_backfill.py), an off-host or credentialed one counted skipped_off_host and an unreadable one skipped_unreadable in the tally, never fetched; tests/test_failure_url_sites_r620.py's backfill case with a login now expects that skip. (S2) skipped_off_host was unbounded (five 9.9 MB urlsets made it 1,191,790 lines, 83 MB): it keeps its first 100 lines (SKIPPED_OFF_HOST_KEPT) beside skipped_off_host_count, and a discovery stops once it has skipped four times max_urls page locs (SKIPPED_LOCS_PER_URL, stopped_reason max_skipped), which is never narrower than before R627, when every loc counted toward max_urls; only kept locs count toward max_urls. (S3) R631's comment said the key was the encoding requests connects with. On the urllib3 the app pins (2.8.0), urllib3 encodes the host first (each label lower-cased, idna.encode(label, strict=True, std3_rules=True)) and requests' UTS 46 path is never reached. The key stays UTS 46 and the wording now says so (crawl.py _site_key, pyproject). Where the two differ (ΣΣ.example, which urllib.parse lowers to σσ and urllib3 label by label to σς; a fullwidth letter; a ligature), R622's _refuse_parser_mismatch refuses the name before any request, held by a test over 3,000 seeded names (2,536 differ, every one refused). (S4) the two tests the read's surviving mutants asked for: the fetcher's refusal of https://u:hunter2@[::1/x carries no password and no chained ValueError, and ingest_url stores and logs none. A nit folded: the site's own key is encoded once (_base_site_key, a cache that only the operator's hosts reach). STATED, not changed: a loc on good.example. (a trailing dot) is off the host, as the host key keeps the dot (R621); health.check_source reports DOWN, not UNKNOWN, for a URL urlparse cannot read (the fetcher's refusal); an on-host loc that redirects off the host is R629's. The test file now holds 99 tests. Release-notes line: «A sitemap no longer widens a source's scope: pages it lists on other sites are skipped and counted, like its child sitemaps. One unreadable link on a page, in a sitemap or in a feed no longer ends that source's whole collection; it is skipped and counted. A site whose name has accented or non-Latin letters keeps the pages its links and sitemaps spell in either form. (R626, R627, R631)»
